## Problem

`package.json:32` uses `"prepublish": "npm run build"`. npm deprecated `prepublish` and it has not run on `npm publish` since npm 5/7. `dist/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:2`) while `main` is `dist/index.js` and `files` is `["README.md","recommended.js","dist/**/*.js"]`. Nothing in the release path builds.

## Evidence

- npm 11.16.0's publish command only fires `prepublishOnly`: `grep -n prepublish $(npm root -g)/npm/lib/commands/publish.js` → `101: event: 'prepublishOnly'`.
- `release-it` config (`package.json:"release-it".npm.publish: true`) runs `npm publish` with no build hook.
- `.gitignore:2` = `dist`, so a fresh clone + `npm run release` publishes with no `dist/` at all; `main` then resolves to a nonexistent file and every consumer's `import '@ivuorinen/stylelint-a11y'` throws ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND.

## Impact

A release cut from a clean checkout publishes a package that cannot be imported. A release cut from a dirty working tree publishes whatever stale `dist/` happens to be on disk — silently shipping old rule code under a new version number.

## Fix

Rename the script to `prepack` (runs on both `npm publish` and `npm pack`):
```json
"prepack": "npm run build",
```
Keep `prebuild: rimraf dist` so the output is always clean. Verify with `npm pack --dry-run` that `dist/**/*.js` appears in the file list.

## Resolution
Renamed prepublish -> prepack. Verified: npm pack --dry-run now ships dist/index.js.
title: prepublish script never runs on npm publish; package ships stale or missing dist/

## Problem

`src/rules/media-prefers-reduced-motion/index.js:164` calls `node.before(media)`, placing the generated `@media screen and (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block *before* the rule it is meant to override. Both rules have identical specificity, so source order decides — and the original rule comes last and wins.

## Evidence

```js
await stylelint.lint({ code: '.a { animation: 1s move; }', fix: true,
  config: { plugins: ['./src/index.js'], rules: {'a11y/media-prefers-reduced-motion': true} } })
```
produces:
```css
@media screen and (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
.a { animation: none;
}
}
.a { animation: 1s move; }
```
`.a` (0,1,0) in the media block, `.a` (0,1,0) after it — the later declaration wins, so `animation: 1s move` still applies with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. Re-linting the fixed output reports no warning, because `check()` only tests for the media block's *presence* among siblings, never its position.

## Impact

`--fix` on the plugin's flagship recommended rule emits CSS that looks compliant, passes its own rule, and does not reduce motion for users who requested it. This is worse than not fixing: it converts a reported violation into a silent one.

## Fix

Insert after the rule instead of before, in `src/rules/media-prefers-reduced-motion/index.js:164`:
```js
node.after(media);
```
Also make `check()` position-aware so the rule reports an override block that precedes its target: compare `parentNodes.indexOf(matchedMediaNode) > parentNodes.indexOf(node)` before accepting. Add a test asserting the fixed output has the `@media` block after the source rule.

## Resolution
Fix now inserts the @media block after the rule (node.after), and check() is position-aware so an override preceding the rule is reported. raws set post-insertion because Root.normalize clobbers raws.before. Tests assert fixed output and re-lint idempotence.
title: --fix inserts the @media override before the offending rule, so the cascade defeats it

## Problem

`jest.config.mjs:13` declares `line: 75` inside `coverageThreshold.global`. Jest reads only `statements`, `branches`, `lines`, `functions`. The key `line` is never looked at and never rejected, so line coverage is unenforced.

## Evidence

`node_modules/@jest/reporters/build/index.js`:
```js
function check(name, thresholds, actuals) {
  return ['statements', 'branches', 'lines', 'functions'].reduce((errors, key) => {
    const threshold = thresholds[key];
    if (threshold !== undefined) { ... }
```
`thresholds['lines']` is `undefined` for this config, so the `if` is skipped entirely. Jest does not warn about unknown threshold keys.

## Impact

`npm run coverage` and the `coverage` CI workflow report a passing gate while one of the four declared thresholds is not checked. CLAUDE.md advertises a "75% threshold"; three of four dimensions actually hold it.

## Fix

`jest.config.mjs:13`:
```js
lines: 75,
```
Confirm the gate is live by temporarily setting `lines: 100` and observing `npm run coverage` fail.

## Resolution
coverageThreshold key corrected to 'lines'. Proved live: temporarily raising it to 100 fails with 'coverage threshold for lines (100%) not met: 97.46%'.
title: coverageThreshold key is 'line', not 'lines' — the line-coverage gate is silently disabled

## Problem

`README.md` "Recommended config" tells users to extend `stylelint-a11y/recommended` and shows the config as containing `"plugins": ["stylelint-a11y"]`. The published package is `@ivuorinen/stylelint-a11y`, and `recommended.js:2` actually contains `plugins: ['.']`. `README.md:15` likewise says to add `stylelint-a11y` to the plugins array.

## Evidence

`recommended.js`:
```js
export default {
  plugins: ['.'],
  rules: { 'a11y/media-prefers-reduced-motion': true, 'a11y/no-outline-none': true, 'a11y/selector-pseudo-class-focus': true },
};
```
vs README:
```json
{ "plugins": ["stylelint-a11y"], "rules": { ... } }
```
The install snippet directly above it (`README.md:8`) correctly says `npm i --dev stylelint @ivuorinen/stylelint-a11y`, so the two halves of the same page disagree on the package name.

## Impact

A user following the README verbatim gets `Could not find "stylelint-a11y". Do you need a `configBasedir`?` from stylelint and has no way to discover the correct specifier from the docs.

## Fix

In `README.md`, replace both occurrences of the bare name with `@ivuorinen/stylelint-a11y`:
- extends target → `@ivuorinen/stylelint-a11y/recommended`
- `README.md:15` → "add `@ivuorinen/stylelint-a11y` to the plugins array"
and replace the JSON block with the actual contents of `recommended.js` (`"plugins": ["."]`), or drop the inline copy and link to the file so the two cannot drift again.

## Resolution
README install/plugins/extends now all say @ivuorinen/stylelint-a11y; the duplicated recommended-config JSON replaced with a link to recommended.js so the two cannot drift.
title: Recommended-config docs name the wrong package and misdescribe recommended.js
no-outline-none misses outline: 0px, outline-style: none and outline-width: 0
Obsolete element/attribute rules use exact whole-selector matching, so almost every real selector bypasses them

## Problem

`package.json` declares `"overrides": { "undici": ">=6.24.0" }`, apparently to force a patched undici. The installed version is 7.24.6, which satisfies `>=6.24.0` and is inside the vulnerable range `7.0.0 - 7.27.2`. The override pins nothing.

## Evidence

```
$ node -p "require('./node_modules/undici/package.json').version"
7.24.6
$ npm audit
undici  7.0.0 - 7.27.2   Severity: high
  GHSA-vmh5-mc38-953g (TLS cert validation bypass via dropped requestTls in SOCKS5 ProxyAgent)
  GHSA-p88m-4jfj-68fv (HTTP header injection via Set-Cookie percent-decoding)
  ... 5 more
js-yaml <=3.14.2 || 4.0.0 - 4.2.0   Severity: high (GHSA-h67p-54hq-rp68, GHSA-52cp-r559-cp3m)
fast-uri  (GHSA-4c8g-83qw-93j6)
5 high severity vulnerabilities
```
`npm audit --omit=dev` reports 0, so nothing reaches consumers — the exposure is the local and CI build environment only.

## Impact

The override reads as active mitigation but permits every vulnerable 7.x. `release-it` uses undici to talk to the npm registry and GitHub during publish, so a compromised proxy or registry response is reachable from the release path — the highest-trust operation this repo performs.

## Fix

Make the override actually exclude the vulnerable range and let `npm audit fix` settle the rest:
```json
"overrides": { "undici": ">=7.27.3" }
```
then `npm install && npm audit` and confirm 0 high. Add `npm audit --audit-level=high` as a gating step in `.github/workflows/tests.yml` so the next drift is caught.

## Resolution
Override tightened to >=7.27.3 and npm audit fix run. npm audit now reports 0 vulnerabilities (was 5 high).
title: undici override is ineffective; 5 high-severity advisories remain open in the dev tree

## Problem

Six rules compute `selector` from an `@page` at-rule's params and then call a `check()` whose first statement discards every non-`rule` node:
```js
function check(selector, node) {
  if (node.type !== 'rule') return true;   // @page always lands here
```
Affected: `content-property-no-static-value/index.js:22`, `no-display-none/index.js:12`, `no-obsolete-attribute/index.js:13`, `no-obsolete-element/index.js:13`, `no-outline-none/index.js:12`, `no-text-align-justify/index.js:12`. Each also has a matching `node.type === 'atrule' && node.name.toLowerCase() === 'page'` branch in its walker that can never lead to a report.

## Evidence

```
SILENT  @page :first { display: none; }
SILENT  @page :first { text-align: justify; }
SILENT  @page :first { content: "x"; }
```
Meanwhile `media-prefers-reduced-motion` and `utils/create-media-query-rule.js` implement the same `@page` branch *without* the early return, so their `@page` handling is live. The codebase carries two contradictory conventions for the same construct.

## Impact

Roughly 8 lines per rule × 6 rules of unreachable code that reads as deliberate `@page` support. A future contributor extending `@page` handling has no way to tell which rules honour it without running each one.

## Fix

Decide one way and apply it uniformly. The lazy correct option is to delete the dead branch — `@page` cannot contain `display`, `text-align: justify` or obsolete selectors in any meaningful sense — replacing the walkers with `root.walkRules()` and dropping the `selector`/`check(selector, node)` plumbing, matching the shape already used by `font-size-is-readable` and `no-important-on-focus`. If `@page` support is wanted instead, remove the `node.type !== 'rule'` early return and add accept/reject `@page` cases to each rule's tests.

## Resolution
Dead @page branch removed from all six rules; they now use root.walkRules like the rest of the plugin. media-prefers-reduced-motion keeps its live @page handling.
title: @page at-rule branch is dead code in six rules

## Problem

`src/rules/media-prefers-reduced-motion/index.js:19`, `:49` and `:71` compare `declaration.prop` against `targetProperties` verbatim:
```js
if (!targetProperties.includes(declaration.prop)) return false;
```
CSS property names are case-insensitive, and every other rule in this plugin normalises with `.toLowerCase()` (e.g. `no-display-none/index.js:18`, `font-size-is-readable/index.js:83`).

## Evidence

```
SILENT  .a { ANIMATION: 2s slide; }
```
with `a11y/media-prefers-reduced-motion: true`. The equivalent lowercase declaration is reported.

## Impact

A stylesheet using uppercase or mixed-case property names — legal CSS, and produced by some generators and minifier round-trips — passes the plugin's flagship recommended rule silently. The same omission also affects `--fix` (`:130`, `:133`), so uppercase declarations are neither reported nor fixed.

## Fix

Normalise at every comparison point in `src/rules/media-prefers-reduced-motion/index.js`. Lines 19, 49, 71:
```js
const prop = declaration.prop.toLowerCase();
if (!targetProperties.includes(prop)) return false;
```
and in the fix block at `:130`/`:133` compare against `o.prop.toLowerCase()`. Add a reject test with `ANIMATION: 2s slide`.

## Resolution
All property comparisons in media-prefers-reduced-motion lowercased, including the fix path. Verified: .a { ANIMATION: 2s slide } is reported and fixed.
title: Property names are not lowercased, so uppercase declarations bypass the rule

## Problem

`src/rules/media-prefers-reduced-motion/index.js:45-56` holds a single `currentSelector` variable that is overwritten as declarations are scanned and stops at the first match `Array.prototype.some` accepts. The whole downstream check (`:74-76`, `checkChildrenNodes` at `:23-25`) then verifies a counterpart for that one property only.

## Evidence

```css
.a { transition: 1s; animation: 2s x; }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .a { transition: none; } }
```
→ `SILENT`. `transition` is matched first, an override for it exists, and `animation: 2s x` is never checked.

## Impact

The most common real shape of this violation — a component that both transitions and animates, where the author remembered only one — reports clean. The rule under-reports precisely where it is most useful.

## Fix

Collect every violating property rather than one, and require all of them to be covered, in `src/rules/media-prefers-reduced-motion/index.js`:
```js
const unmatched = declarations
  .filter((d) => targetProperties.includes(d.prop.toLowerCase()) && d.value !== 'none')
  .map((d) => d.prop.toLowerCase());
if (unmatched.length === 0 || !noMatchedParams) return true;
return unmatched.every((prop) => hasOverrideFor(prop, parentNodes, selector));
```
where `hasOverrideFor` is the existing sibling search parameterised by property. `utils/create-media-query-rule.js:45` already uses exactly this `every`-over-matched-properties shape — reuse it. Add the two-property reject case above as a test.

## Resolution
check() now returns every uncovered property and requires all to be overridden. Verified: transition+animation with only a transition override is reported.
title: Only the first target property is tracked, so one override satisfies a rule with several

## Problem

`src/rules/selector-pseudo-class-focus/index.js:62` short-circuits on a substring test over the whole selector string:
```js
if (selector.indexOf(':hover') >= 0 && selector.indexOf(':focus') >= 0) return;
```
The two pseudo-classes need not belong to the same compound selector — or even to related elements — for this to bail out.

## Evidence

```
SILENT  a:hover, b:focus { color: red; }
```
`a:hover` has no `:focus` counterpart, but the presence of `b:focus` elsewhere in the list satisfies the substring test.

## Impact

A single unrelated `:focus` in a grouped selector suppresses the rule for every `:hover` in that group. Because this rule is in `recommended.js` and is `--fix`-able, the miss is silent in both report and fix modes.

## Fix

Compare per selector rather than over the joined string, in `src/rules/selector-pseudo-class-focus/index.js:62`:
```js
const hovered = rule.selectors.filter((s) => /:hover/i.test(s));
if (hovered.length === 0) return;
if (hovered.every((s) => rule.selectors.includes(s.replace(/:hover/gi, ':focus')))) return;
```
This also subsumes the `hasAlready` same-rule case at `:29`, which currently compares a whole joined selector against `i.selectors` (an array of individual selectors) and so never matches for grouped rules. Add `a:hover, b:focus` as a reject case.

## Resolution
Rewritten to compare per selector via rule.selectors. Verified: a:hover, b:focus is reported and fixes to a:hover, b:focus, a:focus.
title: An unrelated :focus anywhere in a selector list disables the check
Invalid options are reported as a lint warning on the stylesheet instead of failing option validation

## Problem

`src/rules/no-obsolete-element/obsoleteElements.js` lists `'menu'` (line 30) and `'hgroup'` (line 9). Neither is obsolete: `<menu>` is defined in the HTML Living Standard as a semantic alternative to `<ul>` for toolbars, and `<hgroup>` was reinstated and is currently specified for a heading with subordinate content. `<menuitem>` (line 31) *is* obsolete and correctly listed.

## Evidence

```
REPORTED  menu { color: red; }   ::  Unexpected using obsolete selector "menu"
```
Both elements appear in the current HTML specification's element index and neither is in its "Obsolete features" section.

## Impact

Styling a conforming `<menu>` toolbar or an `<hgroup>` heading produces a false accessibility error. Because the rule offers no allow-list option, the only escape is a `stylelint-disable` comment, which also suppresses genuine obsolete-element hits in the same block.

## Fix

Remove both entries from `src/rules/no-obsolete-element/obsoleteElements.js` and drop any accept/reject cases that depend on them in `src/rules/no-obsolete-element/__tests__/index.js`. While there, add a source comment naming the spec section the list tracks so the next audit can re-verify it cheaply.

## Resolution
menu and hgroup removed; a comment records that both are conforming and names the spec section the list tracks.
title: menu and hgroup are flagged as obsolete but are current HTML elements

body:
## Problem

None of the 16 rule modules attach a `meta` object to the exported rule function. Stylelint 17 reads `ruleFunction.meta` for every rule (`node_modules/stylelint/lib/lintPostcssResult.mjs:104`):
```js
postcssResult.stylelint.ruleMetadata[ruleName] = ruleFunction.meta || {};
const shouldWarn = ruleFunction.meta?.fixable && !stylelintOptions.quietDeprecationWarnings;
```
Three rules (`media-prefers-reduced-motion`, `selector-pseudo-class-focus`, `text-spacing-is-readable`) implement `--fix` via `context.fix` but never declare `meta.fixable: true`.

## Evidence

`grep -rn "\.meta\s*=" src/` returns nothing. Consequences observable today:
- `ruleMetadata` is `{}` for every rule, so formatters and editor integrations cannot show a docs link or mark rules fixable.
- Because `meta.fixable` is falsy, `shouldWarn` is false and stylelint's `context.fix` deprecation warning never fires — the deprecation is silently masked rather than addressed. `context.fix` still works (verified: all three fixes apply), but stylelint documents it as deprecated in favour of the `fix` callback on `utils.report`.

## Impact

Consumers get no rule documentation links, `stylelint --fix` cannot be reasoned about from metadata, and the project has no warning signal for the day `context.fix` is removed.

## Fix

Add to each rule module, after the default export:
```js
ruleFunction.meta = {
  url: 'https://github.com/ivuorinen/stylelint-a11y/blob/master/src/rules/<name>/README.md',
  fixable: true, // only on the three fixable rules
};
```
(name the exported function so it can be referenced, or assign `meta` onto the exported const). Extend `src/rules/index.test.js` with an assertion that every rule has `meta.url`, and that `meta.fixable` is set exactly for the three rules the README marks with `-`.

## Resolution
meta.url and meta.fixable attached centrally in src/index.js. The three fixable rules migrated from deprecated context.fix to the report() fix callback, so no deprecation warning is emitted. New src/index.test.js asserts url and fixable for all 16 rules.
title: No rule declares meta, so stylelint 17 cannot report fixability or rule URLs
font-size-is-readable ignores the font shorthand and em/% units
line-height-is-vertical-rhythmed silently skips percentage and em values
no-spread-text only checks ch units, so px/rem/em line lengths are never evaluated

## Problem

`src/rules/text-spacing-is-readable/index.js:75-78` treats an explicit zero as a violation:

    const isZero = value === '0' || parseFloat(value) === 0;
    if (!isZero && !value.endsWith('em')) return;
    if (prop === 'letter-spacing' && parseFloat(value) < minLetterSpacing) { ... }

WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.12 (Text Spacing) does not require authors to *set* 0.12em letter-spacing. It requires that content remain readable and functional when a *user* overrides spacing up to those values. An author writing `letter-spacing: 0` — which is the initial `normal` behaviour for most fonts — is not failing 1.4.12.

## Evidence

    REPORTED  .a { color: red; letter-spacing: 0; }
    ::  Expected letter-spacing to be at least 0.12em in .a

Worse, `--fix` rewrites the declaration:

    in : ".a { color: red; letter-spacing: 0.01em; }"
    out: ".a { color: red; letter-spacing: 0.12em; }"

so running `stylelint --fix` silently changes the visual typography of every text rule that declares any spacing below the threshold.

## Impact

The rule inverts the criterion it cites, then auto-applies the inversion. `letter-spacing: 0` and `letter-spacing: -0.01em` (a normal tracking adjustment for large display text) are both reported, and `--fix` will expand them to 0.12em — a visible, unrequested typographic change justified by a WCAG reference that does not say this.

## Fix

Two options, both requiring a docs change in `src/rules/text-spacing-is-readable/README.md`:

1. Narrow the rule to what 1.4.12 actually constrains — flag declarations that would *prevent* a user override, i.e. spacing set with `!important`, or a negative value large enough to be unreadable — and stop reporting non-negative values below the threshold.
2. Keep the current behaviour but re-document it honestly as an opinionated house-style rule ("require a minimum letter-spacing for body text"), drop the WCAG 1.4.12 citation as its justification, and default the rule to off outside `recommended.js` (it is already excluded there).

Whichever is chosen, exclude `letter-spacing: 0` / `word-spacing: 0` from `--fix` unless the rule is explicitly opted into, so `stylelint --fix` cannot restyle text as a side effect.

## Resolution
Kept the reporting behaviour but --fix no longer rewrites an explicit zero; README documents the reason. Tests use unfixable: true.
title: text-spacing-is-readable reports letter-spacing: 0 as a WCAG 1.4.12 failure, inverting the success criterion

## Problem

All three workflows install with `npm install`, not `npm ci`: `.github/workflows/tests.yml:27`, `.github/workflows/eslint.yml:40`, and implicitly in `coverage.yml` via the action's default. `npm install` resolves semver ranges afresh and may rewrite `package-lock.json`.

## Evidence

Every devDependency in `package.json` is a bare-major range (`"jest": "^30"`, `"eslint": "^10"`, `"stylelint": "^17"`, …), so `npm install` is free to pick any minor or patch published since the lockfile was written. `package-lock.json` is committed but never enforced. `actions/setup-node` is configured with `cache: 'npm'`, which caches by lockfile hash — a cache that a mutating `npm install` can invalidate on its own runs.

## Impact

CI does not test what the lockfile describes. A green build is not reproducible, a newly published malicious or broken patch of any transitive dependency enters CI without review, and a bisect over CI history cannot distinguish a code regression from a dependency drift.

## Fix

Replace with `npm ci` in `.github/workflows/tests.yml:27` and `.github/workflows/eslint.yml:40`. For `coverage.yml`, pass the install command explicitly to the action:
```yaml
- uses: ArtiomTr/jest-coverage-report-action@262a7bb0b20c4d1d6b6b026af0f008f78da72788 # v2.3.1
  with:
    install-command: npm ci
    test-script: npm run coverage
```

## Resolution
npm ci in tests.yml and eslint.yml; install-command: npm ci passed to the coverage action.
title: CI installs with npm install, ignoring the committed lockfile

## Problem

`.github/workflows/tests.yml` has no `permissions:` key at either workflow or job level. The job therefore receives whatever the repository or organisation default is — historically `write-all`, and still settable to that today.

## Evidence

`.github/workflows/eslint.yml:25-27` and `.github/workflows/coverage.yml:9-11` both scope their tokens explicitly; `tests.yml` is the only workflow that does not. The job runs across six matrix legs (`node_version: ['20','22','24']` × `os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest]`) and executes `npm install`, which runs arbitrary lifecycle scripts from the dependency tree.

## Impact

Any dependency install script — or any future step added to this workflow — has whatever token scope the repo default grants. On a `pull_request` from a fork the token is read-only regardless, but on the `push` trigger to `master` it is not: a postinstall script in a compromised transitive dependency could push commits, publish releases, or alter workflow files.

## Fix

Add the least-privilege block at the top of `.github/workflows/tests.yml`, after `on:`:
```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
```
The job only checks out and runs tests, so `contents: read` is sufficient.

## Resolution
Added permissions: contents: read to tests.yml.
title: tests.yml declares no permissions block, so the job runs with the repository default token scope

## Problem

`package.json:29` defines `"pretest": "npm run lint -- --fix"`. npm runs `pretest` before every `npm test`, so running the test suite rewrites source files in place.

## Evidence

`.github/workflows/tests.yml:29` runs `npm test`, which fires `pretest` first. In CI the auto-fixes are applied to the checkout and then discarded, so a lint violation that ESLint can fix is never surfaced by any workflow: `eslint.yml:47` sets `continue-on-error: true` (correctly, so its SARIF upload still runs), and `pretest` fixes rather than fails. Only unfixable violations gate anything.

## Impact

Two distinct problems. Locally, `npm test` is not a read-only operation — it can produce unrelated diffs mid-review or mid-bisect. In CI, fixable lint violations are masked entirely: formatting and `prettier/prettier` errors, which are the majority of what `eslint.config.mjs` enforces, can never fail a build.

## Fix

Drop `--fix` from the pretest hook so the check gates:
```json
"pretest": "npm run lint",
```
and keep fixing as an explicit, separate action (`npm run lint -- --fix`, or the existing `lint-staged` precommit hook at `package.json:26`, which already runs `prettier --write` on staged files).

## Resolution
pretest no longer passes --fix, so fixable lint violations gate instead of being silently rewritten.
title: pretest runs eslint --fix, so npm test mutates the working tree and CI silently rewrites source

## Problem

`eslint.config.mjs:1` imports `@eslint/js`, which is absent from `package.json` — it resolves only because npm hoists it out of `eslint`'s own dependency tree. Conversely `eslint-config-stylelint` and `jest-cli` are declared devDependencies with no reference anywhere in the repo.

## Evidence

```
$ grep -rl <name> --include='*.js' --include='*.mjs' --include='*.json' --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude=package-lock.json .
@eslint/js             -> ./eslint.config.mjs          (not in package.json)
eslint-config-stylelint -> ./package.json only
jest-cli                -> ./package.json only
```
`eslint-config-stylelint` is a shareable ESLint config; `eslint.config.mjs` composes `js.configs.recommended`, `eslint-config-prettier`, `eslint-plugin-prettier` and `eslint-plugin-jest` and never extends it.

## Impact

`npm run lint` breaks the moment ESLint stops depending on `@eslint/js` at the hoisted version, or under a package manager with strict node_modules layout (pnpm, Yarn PnP) — a failure mode that appears only for contributors, never for consumers, and gives a confusing "cannot find module" rather than a dependency error. The two unused packages add install time and audit surface for nothing.

## Fix

```bash
npm install --save-dev @eslint/js
npm uninstall eslint-config-stylelint jest-cli
```
`jest-cli` is redundant with `jest`, which already provides the binary the `test` and `coverage` scripts invoke via `npx jest`. If `eslint-config-stylelint` was meant to be used, add it to the `eslint.config.mjs` array instead of removing it.

## Resolution
@eslint/js added to devDependencies; eslint-config-stylelint and jest-cli removed. eslint exits 0.
title: @eslint/js is a phantom dependency; eslint-config-stylelint and jest-cli are unused

## Problem

`src/rules/selector-pseudo-class-focus/index.js:6` defines a recursive flatten helper:

    const deepFlatten = (arr) => [].concat(...arr.map((v) => (Array.isArray(v) ? deepFlatten(v) : v)));

`Array.prototype.flat` has been available since Node 11; `package.json` requires `node >= 20.19.0`.

## Evidence

The helper's only call site is `:24`, `deepFlatten(nodes).indexOf(...)`, where `nodes` is at most two levels deep — it comes from `parent.nodes.map((i) => { if (i.type === 'rule') return i.selectors; })`. `arr.flat(Infinity)` is exactly equivalent for this input. That same `map` also yields `undefined` for every non-rule sibling, because the arrow has no else branch.

## Impact

A hand-rolled recursion to maintain and cover in place of a built-in, plus `undefined` entries a reader has to rule out as harmless.

## Fix

Delete `deepFlatten` and build the list directly at `:16-24`:

    const selectors = parent.nodes.filter((i) => i.type === 'rule').flatMap((i) => i.selectors);

`filter` before `flatMap` also removes the `undefined` entries. The per-selector rewrite proposed in the "unrelated `:focus`" finding replaces this whole function — apply that one first if both are taken.

## Resolution
deepFlatten deleted; the rewritten rule builds the selector list with filter + flatMap.
title: deepFlatten reimplements Array.prototype.flat

## Problem

`src/rules/animation-duration-reasonable/index.js:11` defines `const DEFAULT_MAX_DURATION_S = 5;` and `:109` hardcodes the same value again as a display string:
```js
message: messages.expected(selector, options?.maxDuration || '5s'),
```

## Evidence

Changing `DEFAULT_MAX_DURATION_S` to, say, `3` changes what the rule enforces but leaves every default-configuration message reading "Unexpected duration greater than 5s" — a message that actively contradicts the behaviour, with no test to catch it (the existing tests assert against the literal `5s` text).

## Impact

Latent documentation drift in user-facing output. Low likelihood, but the failure is silent and lands in the message a user reads while debugging.

## Fix

Derive the string from the constant in `src/rules/animation-duration-reasonable/index.js`:
```js
const DEFAULT_MAX_DURATION_S = 5;
const DEFAULT_MAX_DURATION = `${DEFAULT_MAX_DURATION_S}s`;
...
message: messages.expected(selector, options?.maxDuration || DEFAULT_MAX_DURATION),
```

## Resolution
Message now derives from DEFAULT_MAX_DURATION_S via a single DEFAULT_MAX_DURATION constant.
title: Default max duration is declared twice and can drift out of the message

## Problem

`package.json` declares `"main": "dist/index.js"` with no `"exports"` field. Under Node's legacy resolution that makes every file under `dist/` a supported import path.

## Evidence

`"files": ["README.md", "recommended.js", "dist/**/*.js"]` publishes the full transpiled tree, so `import x from '@ivuorinen/stylelint-a11y/dist/rules/no-outline-none/index.js'` resolves for consumers today. Nothing in the README documents that path, and `src/rules/index.js` is explicitly excluded from coverage as an internal file (`jest.config.mjs:6`).

## Impact

Any internal reorganisation of `src/rules/` becomes a breaking change for whoever happened to deep-import. The package also has no declared entry point for `recommended.js` other than legacy path resolution, so the shareable config's specifier is implicit rather than stated.

## Fix

Add an explicit map to `package.json`:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": "./dist/index.js",
  "./recommended": "./recommended.js",
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
This also lets the README document `extends: "@ivuorinen/stylelint-a11y/recommended"` without the `.js` suffix. Verify with `node -e "import('@ivuorinen/stylelint-a11y/recommended')"` against a `npm pack` tarball.

## Resolution
exports map added with ., ./recommended and ./package.json.
title: No exports map: every internal module path is part of the public API by default

## Problem

`package.json` declares no `types`/`typings` field and the repo contains no `.d.ts` files. The package is plain JavaScript with JSDoc comments that are never emitted as declarations — `.babelrc` runs `@babel/preset-env` only.

## Evidence

    $ node -p "JSON.stringify({types: require('./package.json').types, typings: require('./package.json').typings})"
    {}
    $ ls src/**/*.d.ts
    no .d.ts

`stylelint` itself ships `types/stylelint/index.d.ts` (see its `exports` map), so a TypeScript user configuring stylelint programmatically gets types for everything except this plugin.

## Impact

A TypeScript consumer importing the plugin or `recommended.js` gets `any` with `noImplicitAny` errors under `strict`, and no editor completion for the rule names or option shapes. Nothing breaks at runtime; the cost is entirely developer experience on the public surface.

## Fix

The lazy route, given the codebase is already JSDoc-annotated: emit declarations from the JSDoc rather than hand-writing them.

    npm install --save-dev typescript

`tsconfig.json`:

    { "compilerOptions": { "allowJs": true, "declaration": true, "emitDeclarationOnly": true,
        "outDir": "dist", "module": "esnext", "target": "es2022", "moduleResolution": "bundler" },
      "include": ["src/**/*.js"], "exclude": ["src/**/__tests__/**", "src/**/*.test.js"] }

then `"build": "babel src --out-dir dist && tsc"` and add `"types": "dist/index.d.ts"` to `package.json`. If that is more machinery than wanted, a single hand-written `index.d.ts` declaring the exported plugin array is enough to remove the implicit `any`.

## Resolution
Hand-written types/index.d.ts added (plugin array, rule-name union, per-rule option interfaces), wired via types + exports and added to files.
title: Package ships no type declarations, so TypeScript consumers get an implicit any
The fix path rescans the whole stylesheet for every violation, making --fix quadratic

## Problem

`.github/workflows/coverage.yml:9-11` declares only `checks: write` and `pull-requests: write`. When a `permissions:` block is present, every unlisted permission is set to `none` — including `contents`, which `actions/checkout` (`:14`) needs.

## Evidence

The workflow currently succeeds — `gh run list --workflow=coverage.yml` shows recent runs `completed success` — because checkout of a *public* repository works without a token. The dependency on that fact is invisible in the file.

## Impact

No failure today. If the repository is ever made private or internal, this workflow starts failing at the checkout step with a 403 and no obvious cause: the `permissions` block will look complete because every permission it needs *for reporting* is listed.

## Fix

Add the missing scope in `.github/workflows/coverage.yml`:

    permissions:
      contents: read
      checks: write
      pull-requests: write

## Resolution
Added contents: read to the coverage.yml permissions block.
title: coverage.yml permissions block omits contents, so checkout depends on the repo staying public

## Problem

Recent commits mark GitHub Action major bumps with the conventional-commits breaking marker:
```
b654a0c chore(deps)!: update actions/checkout action (v6.0.2 → v7.0.1) (#16)
0a172e1 chore(deps)!: update actions/setup-node action (v6.3.0 → v7.0.0) (#19)
5dbb654 chore(deps)!: update dependency release-it (19.2.4 → 21.0.0) (#21)
```
None of these changes the published package's behaviour or public API. `actions/checkout` and `actions/setup-node` affect CI only; `release-it` is a devDependency in the release toolchain.

## Evidence

`git show b654a0c --stat` touches only `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The published surface — `dist/`, `recommended.js`, the rule set — is unchanged. The genuine breaking change in this repo's recent history (the stylelint 17 peer requirement and `node >= 20.19.0` engine bump) is not what these markers point at.

## Impact

No version impact today: `package.json`'s `release-it` config declares no conventional-changelog plugin, so the version bump is chosen manually and the `!` marker is decorative. It does mislead a changelog reader into expecting a consumer-visible break, and it would mis-version releases the moment `@release-it/conventional-changelog` is added — which is the natural next step for a repo already writing conventional commits.

## Fix

Reserve `!` for changes to the published package's behaviour, peer range, or supported engines. CI-only and devDependency bumps are plain `chore(deps):` / `chore(ci):`. Since renovate authors these, encode it in `github>ivuorinen/.github:renovate-config` via `semanticCommitType`/`commitMessagePrefix` overrides for the `github-actions` and `devDependencies` package rules rather than fixing them by hand.

## Resolution
Documented in the finding; the convention change belongs in the shared renovate config, not this repo. Left as guidance rather than a code change.
title: Dependency bumps of CI actions are marked as breaking changes

## Problem

`babel src --out-dir dist` compiled every file under `src/`, including
`__tests__/` directories and `*.test.js`. `"files": ["dist/**/*.js"]` then
published all of them.

## Evidence

Before the fix:

    $ npm run build
    Successfully compiled 43 files with Babel
    $ npm pack --dry-run
    npm notice 4.1kB dist/index.test.js
    npm notice total files: 48

The tarball carried the whole test suite — 20 spec files plus their fixtures —
into every consumer's `node_modules`. Commit `fb2de80` ("Drop tests from dist
package, update README") shows this was addressed once before and regressed.

## Impact

Roughly 20 dead files shipped to every consumer, and the published package
exposed `dist/**/__tests__/index.js` as importable paths. Harmless at runtime,
but it inflates install size and publishes files that reference devDependencies
(`testRule`) that consumers do not have.

## Fix

Applied: `package.json` build script now excludes them.

    "build": "babel src --out-dir dist --ignore \"src/**/__tests__/**\",\"src/**/*.test.js\""

Verified: build compiles 23 files instead of 43, `npm pack --dry-run` reports
28 total files instead of 48, and zero paths matching `test`. Guard against a
second regression by asserting the pack contents in CI, or by narrowing `files`
to the exact entry points rather than a `dist/**` glob.

## Resolution
Build now ignores __tests__ and *.test.js. Verified: 23 files compiled (was 43), pack has 28 files (was 48), zero test paths published.
title: Build published the entire test suite into dist/

## Problem

`recommended.js` declared `plugins: ['.']`. stylelint resolves a string entry in
`plugins` from the **consumer's** base directory, not from the directory of the
config file that declares it. In any project extending this config, `'.'`
resolved to the consumer's own project root, which is not a stylelint plugin.

The advertised shareable config therefore failed for every consumer, always.

## Evidence

Packed the real tarball and installed it into a clean project:

    $ cat .stylelintrc.json
    { "extends": "@ivuorinen/stylelint-a11y/recommended" }
    $ npx stylelint t.css
    ConfigurationError: Could not find ".". Do you need to install the package
    or use the "configBasedir" option?
        at getModulePath (node_modules/stylelint/lib/utils/getModulePath.mjs:38:9)
        at toAbsolutePath (node_modules/stylelint/lib/augmentConfig.mjs:185:11)

Both documented forms failed — the programmatic `extends` and the
`.stylelintrc.json` + CLI form. Importing the plugin by bare name
(`plugins: ['@ivuorinen/stylelint-a11y']`) worked, so only the shareable config
was affected.

## Impact

The "Recommended config" section of the README described a feature that could
not work. Anyone following it got a configuration error with no indication that
the fault was in the plugin rather than in their own setup. This is the second
defect in the same paragraph — the package name was also wrong (audit-55e717e5)
— which is likely why the broken plugin path went unnoticed: nobody got far
enough to hit it.

## Fix

Applied. `recommended.js` now imports the plugin array instead of naming a path,
which removes config-relative resolution from the picture entirely:

    import plugins from './dist/index.js';

    export default {
      plugins: [plugins],
      rules: { ... },
    };

Verified end to end against the packed tarball: `npx stylelint t.css` with
`extends: "@ivuorinen/stylelint-a11y/recommended"` now reports both expected
violations. Guarded by the new `npm run smoke` package test, which fails with
`FAIL extends "@ivuorinen/stylelint-a11y/recommended" resolves and reports` when
the old form is restored.

## Resolution
recommended.js now imports the plugin array instead of plugins: ["."]. Verified end to end against the packed tarball; guarded by npm run smoke.
title: The recommended shareable config failed for every consumer

## Problem

Unit tests load rules from `src/`, so no test in this repo exercised the
published artifact. Three separate defects found in this audit were invisible to
the 327-test suite: `prepublish` never running (audit-87f6d40a), the test suite
being published into `dist/` (audit-1dbe412b), and the shareable config failing
for every consumer (the finding above).

## Evidence

All three passed `npm test` and `npm run lint` cleanly. They surfaced only when
the package was packed, installed into a throwaway project, and used the way the
README documents. Commit `fb2de80` ("Drop tests from dist package") shows the
`dist/` defect had already been fixed once and regressed unnoticed.

## Impact

Packaging is the one surface where a defect reaches every consumer at once, and
it was the only surface with no automated check. Each of the three defects would
have shipped in the next release.

## Fix

Applied. Added `scripts/smoke-package.mjs` and an `npm run smoke` script that
packs the package, installs the tarball into a temp project, and asserts:
no test files published, type declarations published, bare-name import exposes
all 16 rules, `extends "@ivuorinen/stylelint-a11y/recommended"` resolves and
reports, `plugins: ["@ivuorinen/stylelint-a11y"]` resolves, and rule metadata
reaches the consumer.

Wired into `.github/workflows/tests.yml` as a single non-matrix step
(ubuntu-latest / node 22) so it costs one job, not six.

Verified the guard actually fails: restoring the old `plugins: ['.']` produces
5 FAIL lines and a non-zero exit.

## Resolution
Added scripts/smoke-package.mjs + npm run smoke, wired into tests.yml. Verified it fails when the defects are reintroduced.
title: No test exercised the published package, hiding three shipped defects

## Problem

mutation-blind. `animation-duration-reasonable` scans every segment of a
comma-separated duration list, but no test exercises a list. The suite is
green whether the loop scans all segments or only the first.

## Evidence

Mutation applied to `src/rules/animation-duration-reasonable/index.js:85`:

    -          for (const segment of segments) {
    +          for (const segment of segments.slice(0, 1)) {

`npx jest src/rules/animation-duration-reasonable` -> SURVIVED (all tests pass).

The behaviour the mutant breaks is correct today, verified by a real lint run:

    .a { animation-duration: 1s, 10s; }
      -> Unexpected duration greater than 5s in .a
    .a { transition-duration: 200ms, 6s; }
      -> Unexpected duration greater than 5s in .a

No `accept` or `reject` case in the test file contains a comma.

## Impact

A regression that stops scanning past the first duration ships silently. CSS
such as `animation-duration: 0.2s, 30s` would lint clean while a 30s animation
plays -- the exact vestibular-trigger case the rule exists to catch
(WCAG 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions).

## Fix

Add to the default-config `testRule` block in
`src/rules/animation-duration-reasonable/__tests__/index.js`:

reject:
  - code: '.foo { animation-duration: 1s, 10s; }'
    message: messages.expected('.foo', '5s')
    description: 'a later segment over the threshold is still caught'
  - code: '.foo { transition-duration: 200ms, 6s; }'
    message: messages.expected('.foo', '5s')
accept:
  - code: '.foo { animation-duration: 1s, 2s, 3s; }'
    description: 'every segment under the threshold'

## Resolution
Added comma-list accept/reject cases to animation-duration-reasonable tests. Proof: re-running the segments.slice(0,1) mutation now KILLS the suite (was SURVIVED). Also added the unitless-maxDuration invalid-option case.
title: Comma-separated duration lists survive a mutation spot-check

## Problem

mutation-blind. `hasObsoleteSelector` only treats `<tag>[attr]` as obsolete
when the sibling compound node is an actual tag. Dropping that guard leaves
the whole suite green.

## Evidence

Mutation applied to `src/utils/obsolete-selectors.js:35-38`:

    -    found = node.parent.nodes.some(
    -      (sibling) =>
    -        sibling.type === 'tag' && obsolete.has(`${sibling.value.toLowerCase()}[${attribute}]`)
    -    );
    +    found = node.parent.nodes.some((sibling) =>
    +      obsolete.has(`${sibling.value.toLowerCase()}[${attribute}]`)
    +    );

`npx jest src/utils` -> SURVIVED.

The guard is load-bearing. Verified against the real function:

    hasObsoleteSelector('.body[link]', new Set(['body[link]'])) === false
    hasObsoleteSelector('body[link]',  new Set(['body[link]'])) === true

and through a real lint run, `.body[link] { color: red }` reports nothing.
Under the mutant, the class node `.body` has `value === 'body'`, so
`body[link]` matches and the selector is reported.

Every existing attribute case in the table uses a bare tag (`a[charset]`,
`body[link]`) or a bare attribute (`[dropzone]`). None pairs an obsolete
attribute with a class or id whose name equals the obsolete tag.

## Impact

A false positive on conforming CSS. `.body[link]`, `#body[link]`, and any
`.font[...]`-shaped selector would be reported as using an obsolete HTML
attribute, and the a11y rule becomes noise the team disables.

## Fix

Add to the `attributes` table in
`src/utils/__tests__/obsolete-selectors.test.js`:

    ['.body[link]', false],
    ['#body[link]', false],

(the `attributes` fixture set already contains `body[link]`), and add an
`accept` case to `src/rules/no-obsolete-attribute/__tests__/index.js`:

    { code: '.body[link] { color: pink; }',
      description: 'a class named like an element does not qualify the attribute' }

## Resolution
Added ['.body[link]', false] and ['#body[link]', false] to the obsolete-selectors attribute table plus matching accept cases on no-obsolete-attribute. Proof: dropping the sibling.type === 'tag' guard now KILLS the suite (was SURVIVED).
title: Tag-qualified attribute guard survives a mutation spot-check

## Problem

coverage-hole. Twelve guard clauses across seven files are live, reachable
code with no test. They are every remaining uncovered branch in the suite.

## Evidence

From `.coverage/coverage-final.json`, uncovered and reachable:

1. `if (!selector) return;` -- animation-duration-reasonable:67,
   font-size-is-readable:99, line-height-is-vertical-rhythmed:73,
   no-important-on-focus:33, no-spread-text:83, text-spacing-is-readable:60.
   Reachable: PostCSS parses `{ color: red }` to a Rule with `selector === ''`,
   and `isStandardSyntaxRule` returns true for it. Verified:
   `parse('{color:red}').walkRules(r => ...)` -> `selector="" std=true`.

2. `if (decl.type !== 'decl') return;` -- animation-duration-reasonable:74,
   font-size-is-readable:104, no-important-on-focus:42,
   text-spacing-is-readable:69. Reachable with a comment child:
   `parse('a { /* c */ font-size: 10px }')` -> child types `comment,decl`.

3. `if (!isStandardSyntaxAtRule(node)) return;` --
   media-prefers-reduced-motion:189, create-media-query-rule:83. Reachable:
   `@page(:first);` parses to `name="page" params="(:first)" afterName=""
   nodes=undefined`, which `isStandardSyntaxAtRule` rejects as a Less
   detached ruleset.

4. `if (!isStandardSyntaxSelector(selector)) return [];` --
   media-prefers-reduced-motion:75, create-media-query-rule:22. Reachable via
   the `@page` arm, which assigns `node.params` to `selector` without a
   pre-check: `@page %x { animation: 1s x; }` gives `stdSel=false`.

5. `if (!declarations) return [];` -- media-prefers-reduced-motion:74,
   create-media-query-rule:20. Reachable: a bodyless at-rule has
   `nodes === undefined`. `parse('@page :first;')` -> `nodes=undefined`.

6. `if (typeof v !== 'string') return false;` -- font-size-is-readable:67.
   Reachable: `{ minSize: 12 }` yields
   `Invalid value "12" for option "minSize"`.

Each was confirmed with a real `stylelint.lint()` run, not by reading.

## Impact

Lower than the mutation-blind findings: these are guards, so a regression
usually surfaces as a crash on non-standard syntax rather than a wrong
verdict. But guard 4 and guard 5 protect the `@page` arm from feeding
`undefined` into `.filter`/`.some`, and a regression there throws inside the
linter -- which stylelint surfaces as a rule crash that aborts the run for
every file, not a warning.

## Fix

Add `accept` cases (all currently lint clean, so they belong in `accept`):

animation-duration-reasonable, font-size-is-readable,
line-height-is-vertical-rhythmed, no-important-on-focus, no-spread-text,
text-spacing-is-readable:
  - `{ <the rule's trigger declaration> }` (empty selector)
  - the same declaration preceded by `/* c */` inside a normal selector

media-prefers-reduced-motion and media-prefers-color-scheme:
  - `@page :first;`
  - `@page %x { <trigger declaration> }`
  - `@page(:first);`

font-size-is-readable, as a separate `testRule` with `config: [true, { minSize: 12 }]`:
  - reject with message
    `Invalid value "12" for option "minSize" of rule "a11y/font-size-is-readable"`

## Resolution
Added accept/reject cases for all twelve guards: empty-selector rules, comment-among-declarations, @page(:first), @page %x, bodyless @page, bodyless nested reduced-motion query, bodyless sibling at-rule, and non-string minSize. Coverage is now 100/100/100/100 and the jest threshold is raised to 100 to hold it. Proof: removing any single new case drops the gate below 100 and jest exits 1.
title: Reachable non-standard-syntax and bodyless at-rule guards have no test

## Problem

tautological. Six test files carry `testRule` blocks introduced to cover an
`@page` / non-rule-node branch that was removed when those rules moved from
`root.walk` to `root.walkRules`. The cases still pass, but not for the stated
reason: `walkRules` never visits an at-rule, so the rule body is never
entered. The test cannot fail for what its comment claims it covers.

## Evidence

`src/rules/no-display-none/__tests__/index.js:50-61`:

    // @page atrule with params (line 39)
    testRule({
      ruleName,
      config: [true],
      accept: [
        { code: '@page :first { margin: 1cm; }',
          description: '@page atrule with params is walked (no display: none)' },
      ],
    });

`src/rules/no-display-none/index.js:26` is `root.walkRules((rule) => {`.
A grep across the plugin confirms only `media-prefers-reduced-motion:179`
still uses `root.walk` with an `@page` arm; the other fourteen rules use
`walkRules`. So the description "is walked" is false for all six.

The same applies to the `// Non-rule node type returns true from check
(line 13)` blocks -- there is no longer a `check` function taking a node type
in these rules.

Affected: no-display-none, no-text-align-justify, no-outline-none,
content-property-no-static-value, no-obsolete-attribute, no-obsolete-element.

Every `(line NN)` reference in these comments is also stale -- e.g.
`// Non-standard syntax rule skipped (line 35)` in no-display-none points at
line 35, which is now inside `messages`.

## Impact

A future contributor reading the suite concludes the `@page` path is covered
for these rules and does not add a test when reintroducing at-rule handling.
The stale line numbers actively misdirect anyone tracing a case back to the
branch it was written for.

## Fix

In each of the six files:
- Delete the `// Non-rule node type returns true from check (line NN)` block,
  or keep the `@media` case and retitle it
  `description: 'rules nested in a media query are still checked'` -- that IS
  what it now exercises.
- Keep the `@page :first { margin: 1cm; }` case (a regression that reinstated
  at-rule walking should not report it) but retitle it
  `description: 'at-rules are not walked by this rule'`.
- Strip every `(line NN)` from the section comments; they are stale and go
  stale again on the next edit.

## Resolution
Retitled the six stale blocks to describe what they now exercise ('an at-rule is not walked by this rule', 'a rule nested in a media query is still checked') and stripped every stale '(line NN)' pointer across seven test files. No tests deleted - the cases still guard against a regression that reinstates at-rule walking.
title: Six test files assert coverage of a code path that no longer exists

## Problem

`createMediaQueryRule` searches *all* siblings of the offending rule for a
counterpart media query (`parentNodes.some(...)`, line 46). It never checks
that the media block comes *after* the rule it is meant to override. Both
carry the same specificity, so a `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block
placed earlier in the source is defeated by the later plain rule and changes
nothing — yet the rule stays silent.

`media-prefers-reduced-motion` already fixes exactly this (it uses
`siblings.slice(index)` in `overriddenProperties`, index passed from
`siblings.indexOf(node)`). The shared helper was not updated with it, so the
two `media-prefers-*` rules built on it still carry the old bug.

## Evidence

Probe run against `src/index.js`:

```css
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { a { color: white; } }
a { color: black; }
```
`a11y/media-prefers-color-scheme` → **silent**.

`a { color: black }` wins the cascade in both light and dark mode; the dark
override is dead. The rule exists to catch precisely this and does not.
Affects `media-prefers-color-scheme` and `media-prefers-contrast`.

## Impact

False negative on the defect the rule was written to detect. A stylesheet
with a cascade-defeated dark-mode override passes lint clean.

## Fix

Mirror the reduced-motion fix in `create-media-query-rule.js`: compute
`const index = parentNodes.indexOf(node)` and search
`parentNodes.slice(index + 1)` instead of `parentNodes`. Add accept/reject
tests for both orderings to
`src/rules/media-prefers-color-scheme/__tests__/index.js` and
`src/rules/media-prefers-contrast/__tests__/index.js`.

## Resolution
create-media-query-rule.js now searches only siblings after the rule (parentNodes.slice(indexOf(node)+1)), matching the reduced-motion fix. Reject test added to media-prefers-color-scheme and media-prefers-contrast; probe confirms the before-order case now reports.

## Problem

`createMediaQueryRule.check` looks for the counterpart media query only among
the rule's *siblings* (`node.parent.nodes`). A `@media` block nested inside
the rule itself is a child, and children are filtered out of the declaration
scan by `declaration.type === 'decl'`. The nested form is therefore invisible
to the rule.

`media-prefers-reduced-motion` handles both forms (its `overriddenProperties`
walks `sibling.nodes` looking for a nested at-rule); the shared helper does
not. Native CSS nesting is Baseline-available and is the form stylelint 17
itself parses without a custom syntax.

## Evidence

Probe run against `src/index.js`:

```css
a { color: black; @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { color: white; } }
```
`a11y/media-prefers-color-scheme` → **REPORTED**.

```css
a { color: black; @media (prefers-contrast: more) { color: white; } }
```
`a11y/media-prefers-contrast` → **REPORTED**.

Both stylesheets are correct and fully satisfy the rule's intent.

## Impact

False positive on correct, modern CSS. A codebase using nesting cannot enable
these two rules at all without blanket-disabling them.

## Fix

In `check()`, before the sibling scan, look for a nested counterpart among
`node.nodes`: an `atrule` child whose `params` contain `mediaFeature` and
whose `nodes` contain a `decl` for the matched property. Treat that as
covering the property. Add accept tests for the nested form to both rules'
`__tests__/index.js`.

## Resolution
Added nestedOverrides() to create-media-query-rule.js; a counterpart nested in the rule itself now covers the property. Accept tests added to both media-prefers-* rules; probe confirms both nested forms are silent.
title: media-prefers-* rules do not understand native CSS nesting and false-positive on it

## Problem

`removesOutline` (line 22) splits the whole value on whitespace and reports a
removed outline if *any* part satisfies `parseFloat(part) === 0`. Modern
space-separated color syntax puts bare numbers in the value, so
`rgb(0 0 0)` contributes the parts `rgb(0`, `0`, `0)` — and `parseFloat('0')`
is `0`.

## Evidence

Probe run against `src/index.js`:

```css
a:focus { outline: 2px solid rgb(0 0 0); }
```
`a11y/no-outline-none` → **REPORTED** ("Unexpected using \"outline\" property").

The comma form is fine, confirming the split is the cause:

```css
a:focus { outline: 2px solid rgb(0,0,0); }
```
→ silent.

Same failure for `hsl(0 0% 0%)`, `rgb(0 0 0 / 50%)`, `lab(0 0 0)`, and any
`color()` value whose first channel is 0.

## Impact

False positive on a correct, visible focus ring written in current CSS Color 4
syntax. Because the rule is in `recommended.js`, every consumer of the
shareable config hits it.

## Fix

Only the outline *width* component can be zero, and it is the part carrying a
length unit or the bare keyword `0`. Restrict the scan to parts outside
function notation — e.g. strip `\w+\([^)]*\)` from the value before splitting:

```js
const parts = value.toLowerCase().trim().replace(/[\w-]+\([^)]*\)/g, '').split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
```

Add accept tests for `rgb(0 0 0)`, `hsl(0 0% 0%)` and `rgb(0 0 0 / 50%)` to
`src/rules/no-outline-none/__tests__/index.js`.

## Resolution
removesOutline now strips function notation (repeated until stable, so nested calls are handled) before splitting on whitespace. Accept tests for rgb(0 0 0), hsl(0 0% 0%) and nested calc; reject test confirms a genuine zero width alongside a function value is still caught.
title: no-outline-none reads space-separated rgb()/hsl() colors as a zero outline width

## Problem

`check()` matches the media-query counterpart with
`selector !== childrenNode.selector` (line 53) — raw string equality on the
whole selector list, including its internal whitespace. PostCSS preserves the
author's spacing in `Rule.selector`, so two selector lists that target exactly
the same elements are treated as different rules.

## Evidence

Probe run against `src/index.js`:

```css
.a,.b { color: black; }
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { .a, .b { color: white; } }
```
`a11y/media-prefers-color-scheme` → **REPORTED**.

The only difference between the two selector lists is the space after the
comma. Adding the space to the first rule makes the report disappear.

## Impact

False positive driven purely by formatting. It fires on stylesheets that are
correct and whose only sin is inconsistent comma spacing — which no formatter
guarantees across a nested-vs-top-level pair.

## Fix

Compare normalized selector lists rather than raw strings. `Rule.selectors`
already splits and trims; compare the sorted arrays:

```js
const norm = (rule) => [...rule.selectors].sort().join(',');
if (!Array.isArray(childrenNodes) || norm(node) !== norm(childrenNode)) return false;
```

`media-prefers-reduced-motion` compares `child.selector === selector` the same
way (lines 58 and 153) and needs the same treatment. Add a test with mismatched
comma spacing to both rules' `__tests__/index.js`.

## Resolution
New src/utils/selectors.js normalizeSelector() trims and sorts the selector list; used by create-media-query-rule.js and by media-prefers-reduced-motion in both overriddenProperties and addOverrides. Accept tests for comma spacing and selector order.
title: Counterpart matching is exact selector-string equality, so whitespace variance false-positives

## Problem

`check()` accepts a `content` declaration only when its value is `''`, `""`,
or `attr(aria-label)` (lines 31-33). `none` and `normal` are neither
generated content nor an accessibility hazard — `content: none` *removes* the
pseudo-element, which is the standard way to cancel an inherited `::before`.

## Evidence

Probe run against `src/index.js`:

```css
a::before { content: none; }
```
`a11y/content-property-no-static-value` → **REPORTED**
("Unexpected using \"content\" property in a::before").

No text is injected into the accessibility tree by this declaration; there is
nothing for a screen reader to read out.

## Impact

False positive on the idiomatic way to suppress a pseudo-element. Authors must
add a disable comment to cancel decoration they did not add.

## Fix

Add the two no-op keywords to the accepted set in `check()`:

```js
const ACCEPTED = new Set(["''", '""', 'attr(aria-label)', 'none', 'normal']);
...
ACCEPTED.has(o.value.toLowerCase().trim())
```

Add accept tests for `content: none` and `content: normal` to
`src/rules/content-property-no-static-value/__tests__/index.js`.

## Resolution
Accepted content values moved to an acceptedValues Set that now includes none and normal; value is trimmed before lookup. Accept tests added; content: 'hi' still reported.

## Problem

`declaredSelectors(rule.parent)` (line 45) walks every sibling rule and
flat-maps its `selectors`, and the result is rebuilt inside the `walkRules`
callback — once for every rule carrying a `:hover` selector. For a stylesheet
where most rules have a hover state this is O(n²) in the number of sibling
rules. The set depends only on `rule.parent`, not on `rule`.

An earlier audit fixed the quadratic *fix* path (`audit` resolved finding
"The fix path rescans the whole stylesheet for every violation"). The *check*
path was not changed and is still quadratic.

## Evidence

Timed against `src/index.js`, a flat stylesheet of `.rN:hover{color:red}`
rules, `a11y/selector-pseudo-class-focus` alone:

| rules | time |
| ----- | ---- |
| 500   | 154 ms |
| 1000  | 412 ms |
| 2000  | 1811 ms |
| 4000  | 8561 ms |

Each doubling of `n` roughly quadruples the time — the signature of O(n²).
By comparison `media-prefers-color-scheme` on the same shape runs 14/29/87 ms
at 500/1000/2000.

8.5 seconds for one rule on a 4000-rule stylesheet is a visible editor and CI
cost; the rule is in `recommended.js`, so every consumer of the shareable
config pays it.

## Impact

Lint time grows quadratically with stylesheet size on a rule that is on by
default. Large design-system stylesheets (a few thousand rules is ordinary)
spend seconds in this one rule.

## Fix

Cache the declared-selector set per parent instead of recomputing it per rule.
A `WeakMap` keyed on the parent node, built once inside the returned rule
function, keeps it O(n):

```js
const cache = new WeakMap();
const declaredFor = (parent) => {
  let set = cache.get(parent);
  if (!set) {
    set = new Set(declaredSelectors(parent));
    cache.set(parent, set);
  }
  return set;
};
```

The `fix` callback mutates `rule.selector`, so invalidate (or add to) the
cached set inside the fix rather than leaving it stale. Add a test asserting
a second `:hover` rule in the same parent is still reported after the first
one is fixed.

## Resolution
Declared-selector set cached in a per-run WeakMap keyed on the parent, with the fix path adding the selectors it declares so the cache cannot go stale. Measured 4000 rules: 8561 ms -> 77 ms; 2000: 1811 -> 47; 1000: 412 -> 41. Fix output verified still idempotent.
title: selector-pseudo-class-focus rebuilds the sibling selector set per rule, making the check quadratic

## Problem

`textStyles` (line 2) is a named export of `src/utils/text-helpers.js`. No
production module imports it — its only consumer is
`src/utils/__tests__/text-helpers.test.js`, which asserts the array's
contents directly.

## Evidence

```
$ grep -rn "textStyles" src/ --include=*.js | grep -v src/utils/text-helpers.js
src/utils/__tests__/text-helpers.test.js:1:import { textStyles, nodesProbablyForText } ...
src/utils/__tests__/text-helpers.test.js:5:    expect(textStyles).toContain('color');
...
src/utils/__tests__/text-helpers.test.js:12:    expect(textStyles).not.toContain('display');
```

The assertions restate the literal a few lines above them — `toContain('color')`
against a list whose source is `['text-decoration', ..., 'color']`. They fail
only if someone edits the list, which is the change they are supposed to
permit; they cannot fail for any behavioral reason.

## Impact

Two small costs, no benefit: an internal constant is part of the module's
export surface for no consumer, and four tests contribute assertion count and
coverage without testing behavior.

## Fix

Drop the `export` keyword from `textStyles` and delete the `describe('textStyles')`
block. The behavior that matters is already covered by the
`nodesProbablyForText` tests in the same file, which exercise the list through
its actual caller.

## Resolution
textStyles is no longer exported; the describe('textStyles') block was replaced with it.each cases that exercise the list through nodesProbablyForText, its actual caller.
title: textStyles is exported only for its own test to assert on

## Problem

`docs/audit/arch-profile.md` exists so later `arch` runs check violations
against it instead of re-deriving the pattern. Its "Known divergences" section
describes three things that are no longer true — it was written before the
findings it cites were fixed, and was not refreshed when they were.

> No rule declares a `meta` object, so the plugin exposes no rule URLs and no
> `fixable` flag to stylelint's metadata surface. See finding `audit-8a3c3b68`.

`src/index.js` has declared it since that finding was resolved:

```
$ grep -n "meta" src/index.js
22:  rule.meta = {
23:    url: `${DOCS_BASE}/${ruleName}/README.md`,
24:    fixable: FIXABLE.has(ruleName),
25:  };
```

`audit-8a3c3b68` is in `resolved.jsonl` as `fixed`
("No rule declares meta, so stylelint 17 cannot report fixability or rule URLs").

The profile also states six rules carry an unreachable `@page` branch
(citing `audit-22c61a04`, also resolved as `fixed`). Those rules now use
`root.walkRules`; the only surviving `@page` branches are the two live ones,
in `create-media-query-rule.js` and `media-prefers-reduced-motion/index.js`:

```
$ grep -rn "name === 'page'" src/ --include=*.js | grep -v __tests__
src/utils/create-media-query-rule.js:82
src/rules/media-prefers-reduced-motion/index.js:188
```

## Impact

The profile is the input a future `/nitpicker arch` run trusts. As written it
would flag already-fixed issues and mis-describe the convergence target,
producing duplicate findings against current code.

Refresh `docs/audit/arch-profile.md`:

- Delete the `meta` paragraph; record instead that `src/index.js` assigns
  `meta.url` and `meta.fixable` centrally from the `FIXABLE` set, which is
  the current pattern a new rule must follow.
- Replace the `@page` bullet with the state that actually diverges now: two
  independent implementations of the same "rule needs a media-query
  counterpart" check — `utils/create-media-query-rule.js` (shared by
  `media-prefers-color-scheme` and `media-prefers-contrast`) and
  `media-prefers-reduced-motion/index.js`. Findings `audit-81697e2a`,
  `audit-f3de4e79` and `audit-8c8dc39d` are all consequences of the two
  copies drifting apart, which makes converging them the live architectural

## Resolution
arch-profile.md refreshed: stale meta and @page paragraphs replaced with a Rule metadata section describing the FIXABLE-driven central assignment, and a Known divergences section naming the real live divergence (two copies of the counterpart search). body:
## Problem

`jest.config.mjs` holds statements, branches, functions and lines at 100 and
the suite meets it — 20 suites, 359 tests, every file at 100% across all four
counters. Six behavioral defects in the rules survive that gate untouched,
because the suite exercises every *line* while asserting almost nothing about
CSS shapes the rules will actually meet.

The gate's comment claims "The suite covers every reachable statement and
branch in `src/`", which is true and also not what a lint plugin needs to be
correct. Coverage here is measuring the wrong thing, and its being pinned at
100 reads as much stronger assurance than it provides.

## Evidence

Full suite green at 100% coverage:

```
Test Suites: 20 passed, 20 total
Tests:       359 passed, 359 total
```

Six defects confirmed by probe against the same `src/` the suite covers,
none of which any test catches:

| Finding | Missing case |
| --- | --- |
| `audit-81697e2a` | media-prefers-* override placed *before* the rule |
| `audit-dd2bb4e9` | nested reduced-motion block in an unrelated sibling |
| `audit-f3de4e79` | native CSS nesting form of the counterpart media query |
| `audit-d94132ba` | `outline: 2px solid rgb(0 0 0)` — space-separated color |
| `audit-8c8dc39d` | `.a,.b` vs `.a, .b` selector-list whitespace |
| `audit-e39e660e` | `content: none` / `content: normal` |

Every one is a value or source-order shape, not a new code path — so each is
invisible to a line/branch counter that is already saturated.

## Impact

The 100% gate gives a false read on suite quality and blocks nothing that
matters: a rule can be rewritten to produce wrong verdicts and still pass, so
long as the same statements execute. New contributors will trust the number.

## Fix

Keep the gate (it does stop dead code accruing) but stop treating it as the
quality signal. Concretely:

1. Add an accept/reject case per row of the table above, in the corresponding
   rule's `__tests__/index.js`, as part of fixing each finding.
2. Add a shared fixture set of realistic CSS shapes every rule is run
   against — source order variants, native nesting, CSS Color 4 functions,
   selector-list spacing — so the next value-shape gap fails a test rather
   than sitting under a green 100%.
3. Reword the `coverageThreshold` comment so it claims what it measures
   (no unexercised code) rather than suite completeness.

## Resolution
Added 25 accept/reject cases covering all six value/source-order shapes plus the three parser-edge guards they exposed (bodyless nested at-rule, comment in a media block, non-decl in a nested block). Suite 359 -> 384 tests, still 100% on all four counters. coverageThreshold comment reworded to state what the number measures and that behavioural coverage belongs in the per-rule cases.
title: 100% coverage gate passes while six confirmed rule defects go undetected

## Problem

`toFocus` (line 12) is a blind `selector.replace(/:hover/gi, ':focus')`. It has
no idea whether the `:hover` it rewrites is the subject of the selector or an
argument to a functional pseudo-class. For `:not(:hover)` the substitution
inverts the meaning of the selector, and the rule then *appends* the result to
the selector list as an auto-fix.

## Evidence

Probe against `src/index.js`, `--fix` on:

```css
.a:not(:hover) { color: red; }
```
produces

```css
.a:not(:hover), .a:not(:focus) { color: red; }
```

`.a:not(:focus)` matches every `.a` on the page that is not currently focused —
which, on a page with at most one focused element, is essentially all of them.
The declaration block that was scoped to non-hovered elements now applies
almost unconditionally. `--fix` silently restyles the page.

`:has()` takes the same path: `.a:has(:hover)` becomes
`.a:has(:hover), .a:has(:focus)`.

The rule should not have fired at all: `:not(:hover)` styles the *absence* of
hover, a state with no focus counterpart to require.

## Impact

An auto-fix that changes rendered output on correct input — the worst class of
lint bug, because `--fix` is normally run unattended in a pre-commit hook or
CI. The report itself is also a false positive.

## Fix

Only consider `:hover` that is not inside a functional pseudo-class argument.
Parse with `postcss-selector-parser` (already a dependency, already used by
`utils/obsolete-selectors.js`) and skip a `:hover` whose ancestor chain
includes a `pseudo` node with `nodes` — i.e. any `:not()`, `:is()`, `:where()`,
`:has()` argument. Rules whose only `:hover` is inside such an argument are
neither reported nor fixed.

Add accept tests for `.a:not(:hover)`, `.a:is(:hover)` and `.a:has(:hover)`,
and keep the existing `.a:hover` reject case as the control.

## Resolution
hasSubjectHover now parses the selector and ignores any :hover nested inside a functional pseudo-class. Verified --fix leaves .a:not(:hover) and .a:has(:hover) untouched while .a:hover still gains .a:focus. The guarded parse was extracted to utils/selectors.js someSelectorNode rather than duplicated, so obsolete-selectors.js and this rule now share one parse site.
title: The fix rewrites :hover inside functional pseudo-classes, broadening the selector to match almost everything

## Problem

CSS media feature names are ASCII case-insensitive. `isReducedMotion`
(line 24) tests `node.params.indexOf(MEDIA_FEATURE) >= 0` and
`uncoveredProperties` (line 82) tests `params.indexOf(MEDIA_FEATURE) >= 0`,
both against the raw string. `utils/create-media-query-rule.js` lowercases
first (`node.params.toLowerCase().includes(mediaFeature)`), so the two
implementations of the same check disagree.

This is the divergence `docs/audit/arch-profile.md` records: a property fixed
in one copy of the counterpart search and not the other.

## Evidence

Probe against `src/index.js`. Uppercase override is not recognised:

```css
.a { animation: spin 1s; }
@media (PREFERS-REDUCED-MOTION: REDUCE) { .a { animation: none; } }
```
`a11y/media-prefers-reduced-motion` → **REPORTED** (should be silent).

A rule already inside an uppercase block is not recognised as being the
override itself:

```css
@media (PREFERS-REDUCED-MOTION) { .a { animation: spin 1s; } }
```
→ **REPORTED** (should be silent).

The equivalent for the shared factory is already correct:

```css
a { color: black; }
@media (PREFERS-COLOR-SCHEME: DARK) { a { color: white; } }
```
`a11y/media-prefers-color-scheme` → silent.

## Impact

False positives on valid CSS, and the rule cannot be silenced by writing a
correct override — the author has to lowercase their media query to satisfy
it. Two rules that should behave identically do not.

## Fix

Lowercase before comparing in both places, matching the factory:

```js
const isReducedMotion = (node) =>
  node && node.type === 'atrule' && !!node.params &&
  node.params.toLowerCase().includes(MEDIA_FEATURE);
```

and in `uncoveredProperties`:

```js
if (params && params.toLowerCase().includes(MEDIA_FEATURE)) return [];
```

Add accept tests for both uppercase shapes above.

## Resolution
isReducedMotion and the already-inside-a-block check both lowercase params before comparing, matching create-media-query-rule.js. Accept tests added for the uppercase override and the uppercase enclosing block.
title: media-prefers-reduced-motion matches media params case-sensitively, unlike the shared factory

## Problem

`textStyles` is the list that decides whether a rule "is probably for text".
It contains `text-decoration`, `text-align`, `text-transform`, `text-indent`,
`letter-spacing`, `line-height`, `direction`, `word-spacing`, `text-shadow`,
`text-overflow` and `color` — and no font property at all. `font`,
`font-size`, `font-family` and `font-weight` are all absent, as are
`white-space`, `word-break` and `hyphens`.

`nodesProbablyForText` gates two rules: `no-spread-text` and
`text-spacing-is-readable`. A rule whose only text signal is a font property
is invisible to both.

## Evidence

Probe against `src/index.js`:

```css
.a { max-width: 20ch; font-size: 16px; }
```
`a11y/no-spread-text` → **silent** (20ch is below the 45-character minimum).

```css
.a { max-width: 20ch; font-family: serif; }
```
→ **silent**.

Control, identical except the text signal is a listed property:

```css
.a { max-width: 20ch; color: red; }
```
→ **REPORTED**.

Setting `font-size` is a stronger signal that a rule styles text than setting
`color`, which applies to borders and backgrounds of non-text boxes too.

## Impact

`no-spread-text` misses measure violations on the most idiomatic way to write
a text block (`max-width` plus `font-size`). The gate is meant to suppress
noise on non-text rules; instead it suppresses the rule's primary use case.

## Fix

Add the font and text-flow properties to `textStyles`:

```js
'font',
'font-family',
'font-size',
'font-weight',
'font-style',
'white-space',
'word-break',
'hyphens',
```

Add accept/reject cases to both rules' `__tests__/index.js` covering a rule
whose only text signal is `font-size`.

## Resolution
textStyles gained font, font-family, font-size, font-style, font-weight, white-space, word-break and hyphens. no-spread-text now reports max-width: 20ch beside font-size or font-family; a rule with no text signal at all is still skipped.
title: textStyles omits every font property, so text rules are not recognised as text

## Problem

Line 76 reads `if (!isZero && !value.endsWith('em')) return;`. Any
`letter-spacing` or `word-spacing` written in `px`, `rem`, `pt` or any other
absolute unit is dropped before the threshold comparison. The rule's stated
contract is a minimum of `0.12em`/`0.16em`; nothing in the README says the
check applies only to values already written in `em`.

## Evidence

Probe against `src/index.js`:

```css
.a { color: red; letter-spacing: 1px; }
```
→ **silent**.

At the 16px default root size, `1px` is `0.0625em` — roughly half the `0.12em`
threshold the rule exists to enforce. The control confirms the threshold works
for `em`:

```css
.a { color: red; letter-spacing: 0.2em; }
```
→ silent (above threshold), and `0.01em` → REPORTED.

`src/rules/text-spacing-is-readable/README.md` states only "Require readable
text spacing (letter-spacing >= 0.12em, word-spacing >= 0.16em)". A reader
enabling this rule on a px-based stylesheet gets no coverage and no warning
that they got none.

## Impact

The rule reports nothing on stylesheets that author spacing in `px` — a large
share of real CSS. It reads as passing when it is simply not looking.

## Fix

Convert absolute units to `em` against the 16px root assumption already used
by `no-spread-text` (`ROOT_FONT_SIZE_PX`), and keep skipping only what cannot
be resolved statically (`%`, `calc()`, custom properties, viewport units):

```js
const EM_PER_PX = 1 / 16;
const toEm = (value) => {
  const number = parseFloat(value);
  if (!Number.isFinite(number)) return null;
  if (value.endsWith('em')) return number;      // rem handled the same way
  if (value.endsWith('px')) return number * EM_PER_PX;
  return null;
};
```

Document the conversion and the 16px assumption in the rule README, as
`no-spread-text` already does for its own heuristic. Add reject tests for
`letter-spacing: 1px` and `word-spacing: 1px`, and accept tests for
`letter-spacing: 3px` (0.1875em, above threshold) and `max-width`-style
unresolvable values.

## Resolution
New toEm() converts px and pt against a 16px root and returns null for anything unresolvable, replacing the endsWith('em') early return. letter-spacing: 1px and word-spacing: 1px now report; 3px and 3pt pass; %, calc() still skipped. Units section added to the rule README.
title: text-spacing-is-readable silently skips every non-em length, contradicting its own threshold
